triggerReasons.message: High-risk or gate/security wording selects high-assurance intent hardening.
High-assurance work requires an independent intent-collision result.
Ambiguity, user impact, behavior change, or multi-deliverable intent makes intent collision diagnostically required.
Bug, regression, security/auth/session, benchmark, or explicit behavior-change work should have red evidence.
Broad or absolute scope wording should have scope clarification before future enforcement.

acceptanceBindings.acceptanceClaim: On the fixed tree, every malformed red-evidence artifact - malformed record, malformed envelope, non-object JSON root, or unparseable file - produces a controlled typed outcome rather than a bare TypeError or a silent misread as absent evidence, while the pinned five-scenario v1 invariance digest 2d584cc157e83ebb2f8396735f04d46946f0ba90d18a55d9fb2f263d706a11ec is unchanged.
acceptanceBindings.note: Corruption is detected and reported rather than crashing: the repro pins all three defect classes pre-fix, and the read-boundary validator turns each into a controlled typed outcome, validating the envelope before the records.

acceptanceBindings.note: The failure stays diagnosable and repairable end to end: the predicate never throws even when bypassed, every consumer renders corruption distinctly from absence rather than aborting or degrading to 'not configured', and the verdict no longer depends on array position.

acceptanceBindings.note: The guarantee holds beyond the enumerated rows: the validator is total on generated arbitrary JSON, not just on the shapes that were observed failing, and the decision record that defines all of this is landed so the claim is auditable independently.

acceptanceBindings.note: Nothing that was already correct changed: the invariance digest is pinned pre-fix and asserted unchanged post-fix, v2 records and absent-records artifacts keep their existing behaviour, and the migration scan proves no real record that satisfies the gate today is reclassified.

note: Splits the single acceptance claim into the four sub-claims that can independently fail, so partial delivery cannot be reported as success. AB-1 to AB-3 are the positive half (each corruption class becomes controlled); AB-4 is the negative half (nothing that was correct changed). Every checklist item appears in exactly one binding.
